victory.title: Wartime / Victory house
victory.form: Detached house, one full storey plus occupied attic
victory.description: A compact home with a steep roof, shallow eaves and simple openings. Wartime housing programmes helped provide homes for defence workers and returning veterans. This original teaching design illustrates the form; it does not copy a particular historic house.
lookFor: Attic windows in the end gables
victory.designQuestion: How could this small home accommodate change while retaining its useful existing structure?
victory.componentLimit: The isolated house does not establish a street layout, current affordability, ownership or a complete housing programme.
victory.evidenceBasis: Primary historical context plus exact original generated reference pixels; metric size and internal plan inferred.

split.title: Postwar side-split house
split.form: Detached house with staggered living, lower and upper levels
split.designPeriod: 1950s to 1970s association; split-levels appear in CMHC's 1954 catalogue
split.description: A split-level offsets parts of the house by a short stair flight. Here the living wing meets raised bedrooms and a lower recreation level. Split-level is a form, while the picture window, simple roofs and restrained siding express this example's mid-century aesthetic.
lookFor: A low living wing beside a raised sleeping wing
Picture window and restrained brick/siding palette
split.designQuestion: How do the staggered levels affect daily movement and the possibilities for adapting the home?
split.componentLimit: A split-level does not establish car dependence or tenure. Its internal stairs create access questions; no accessibility compliance is claimed.
split.evidenceBasis: CMHC 1954 catalogue establishes the historical form. Exact exterior follows an original generated design; dimensions and internal plan are inferred.
